races.name: Sligo Plumb Centre Mares Maiden Hurdle

runners_data.name: Belladaball
runners_data.note: Gavin Cromwell's 5-year-old holds the joint-top OR of 120 and has winning form on Good ground over hurdles, but her natural racing style sits firmly at the back of the field — in a race with only one true pace-setter she is unlikely to find the truly searching gallop her hold-up game depends on, which tempers confidence.

runners_data.name: Cotswold Blue
runners_data.note: Won last time over 16f on Good for W P Mullins, Mr P W Mullins up again, and a 100% record in 3 similar-going runs — she is the sole confirmed front-runner and the course and conditions are a perfect fit.

runners_data.name: Searcog
runners_data.note: Patrick Magee's 4-year-old has placed at 18f on Good and has the most recent run (10 days), but genuine closing style makes her reliant on a pace she's unlikely to get here; her 1W3P sim-going record shows consistency without a dominant recent run.

runners_data.name: Carleys Lilly
runners_data.note: Has placed at 18f on Good ground and was 3rd at this trip 13 days ago, giving her live claims on form — but like Belladaball she races off the pace naturally and will be searching for gaps in a field where the pace is too moderate to fully suit.

runners_data.name: Granny For Sport
runners_data.note: Complete unknown on style and going — no recent form string, lightly raced, and a debut or near-debut runner, which makes her impossible to place accurately but also means she carries no negative form baggage; Ross O'Sullivan is capable of producing a first-time-out type.

runners_data.name: Jolly D'olivate
runners_data.note: The finish-fading flag is a significant concern for a 7-year-old in a 2m1½f hurdle; three recent efforts on Good all ended in double-figure finishes and P J Rothwell's 2/30 14-day strike rate offers little trainer confidence.

runners_data.name: Nelliestar
runners_data.note: A dire recent form string — single hurdles run ending 10th, preceded by low-grade flat efforts — and the fades-in-finish flag combine to make her a very tough sell on any scenario; Tom McGettigan's stable is cold at 0/3 in the last 14 days.

runners_data.name: Tubberfinn Lassie
runners_data.note: The unclassified style and lightly-raced tag mean her tactics are unknown, but her only hurdles run was a 7th on Good over 18f — she at least has trip form on the going and ran 10 days ago, suggesting connections are happy with her current condition.

runners_data.name: Moonwing
runners_data.note: Four-year-old with two runs both ending 11th on Good ground, and the fades-in-finish flag makes it hard to see how this trip and pace shape unlocks improvement; Paul John Gilligan's yard is winless in 6 recent starts.

races.paceDynamic: Cotswold Blue is the sole confirmed front-runner here and, with no genuine rival for the lead, Mr P W Mullins can dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop from the front over 2m1½f on Good ground at Sligo — a tight, turning track that rewards travelling well and jumping fluently. With Belladaball, Carleys Lilly, and Searcog all tagged as true hold-up types redistributed into midfield on the map, the field holds more off-the-pace horses than the race shape can genuinely accommodate at the rear, meaning Cotswold Blue's uncontested lead is essentially guaranteed. The field holds more prominent/hold-up types than can all settle into their natural positions — Belladaball, Carleys Lilly, and Searcog are the most likely to try to press forward but none are natural front-runners, so some tactical friction in the pack is likely even if the lead itself is uncontested. A race run at a comfortable front-runner's tempo with a clear leader strongly favours a horse that can travel prominently, jump well, and kick from the front rather than those who need a truly searching pace to close into.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Cotswold Blue Controls
scenarios.trigger: If Cotswold Blue secures the lead unchallenged and dictates a fair, unhurried pace through the early stages.
scenarios.body: W P Mullins's 6-year-old settles into a rhythm and uses Sligo's turning track to stay balanced, arriving at the last with petrol in the tank; Good ground and three recent placings at this trip make this the path of least resistance.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Closers Strike
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is just strong enough to stretch the field and leave a gap for the better-quality hold-up mares to close into.
scenarios.body: Belladaball has the highest OR in the field and her single Hurdles win came on Good ground over a similar trip, meaning if she can travel sweetly mid-pack and pick up late she is the most dangerous closer; Carleys Lilly has placed at this distance on Good and would also benefit from any late-race attrition.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Mares Rally
scenarios.trigger: If Cotswold Blue's pace fades in the final half-mile and a horse tracking just behind can pounce at the last.
scenarios.body: A mare sitting two or three lengths off the leader in the slipstream can exploit a tiring front-runner without needing a sustained finishing burst; Granny For Sport and Tubberfinn Lassie are both unknowns whose style is unclassified, giving them some tactical flexibility if they travel well.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If the moderate pace produces a muddled, slowly-run affair that turns into a sprint from the second-last.
scenarios.body: In a messy finish on a tight track the advantage shifts entirely to the horse with the best jumping technique and most tactical awareness at the obstacles; Cotswold Blue's jumping record and W P Mullins's course intelligence still give her an edge even in this chaos scenario.

watchPoints.text: Cotswold Blue jumps efficiently at the front — watch whether Mr P W Mullins allows her to stride on or deliberately settles, as any change in tempo approaching the final bend will dictate the outcome for every other runner.

Belladaball and Carleys Lilly are both true hold-up mares forced toward the middle of the pack in running — watch for positional shuffling behind the leader in the first mile that could cause interference or cost them lengths at a crucial stage.

Granny For Sport is a total unknown on style — watch the early strides to see whether Danny Gilligan pushes her forward to chase Cotswold Blue or settles back; her tactical position will determine which scenario she feeds into.

Searcog has the freshest recent appearance (10 days) among the prominent hold-up types and ran 2nd on Good over 18f — watch whether Eoin Walsh elects to track the leader rather than settle deep, which would be out of role but more competitive given the pace shape.
Going is Good throughout the card at Sligo — no deterioration reported, so no horse gains or loses ground-related advantage as the card progresses; pace and jumping will be the decisive factors.

races.name: Aidan Moffitt Memorial Handicap Hurdle

runners_data.name: Fremantle Doctor
runners_data.note: Hold-up type trained by McConnell; 9 days since a solid placed effort on good ground and the sim-going record of 0W3P shows consistent involvement without winning — a patient ride from O'Brien could see him factor late if pace is honest.
runners_data.comment: Fremantle Doctor ran a fine second last time out and returns quickly on nine days' rest, with experience of today's trip and going working in his favour; the main concern is a hefty 168 lb to carry for a gelding yet to win in his last five starts.

runners_data.name: William F Browne
runners_data.note: The sole front-runner here; Williamson takes over on this 4yo for Flynn, who has had no winners in 14 days, and blinkers are fitted — he sets the tempo for everyone but a career record of 0W1P on similar going and an OR of 99 suggest he is vulnerable if headed.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last four starts and ranked seventh of thirteen on our rating, William F Browne faces an uphill task; a refusal in recent outings is a concern, and a struggling trainer adds little confidence, though he has run over today's trip and going before.

runners_data.name: Alentejo
runners_data.note: McNiff's 5yo carries a finish-fade flag that is a genuine concern in a slowly-run affair; 16 days fresh, turf headgear retained, but sim-going record of 0W0P from 4 qualified runs and a tendency to weaken late make this a difficult conveyance in any scenario.
runners_data.comment: Alentejo has run over today's trip and going before, but his recent record gives cause for concern — pulled up last time out and winless in his last four starts, carrying 163 lb makes life harder still for a gelding ranked fifth of thirteen.

runners_data.name: Tradonthebay
runners_data.note: Prominent racer for the Gilligan yard; the 5yo has placed twice from nine runs on good turf and was a solid second last time on 20f good ground, suggesting the 2m1½f trip and conditions are both comfortably within range — likely to track William F Browne closely.
runners_data.comment: Third two starts back and a runner-up five starts back, Tradonthebay arrives here just 18 days on from his last outing with both distance and going experience to call on, though he has to overcome a disappointing ninth last time and carries 162 lb.

runners_data.name: High Honour
runners_data.note: Kinsella's 6yo has not run for 68 days and carries a finish-fade concern; sim-going figures of 0W2P across 10 qualifying runs tell a story of involvement without resolution, and the lengthy absence makes it hard to trust at this level.
runners_data.comment: High Honour holds the top rating in the field and has distance and going experience to call on, with a third three starts back hinting at ability, yet he is winless in his last four starts and a pulled-up latest effort raises stamina or fitness questions at 68 days off.

runners_data.name: Bowgate Street
runners_data.note: O'Keeffe partners this 7yo who boasts 14 qualified sim-going runs at 1W4P — more good-ground experience than almost any rival; the 26-day freshener looks fine and a win at 18f on good turf last season marks him as the primary hold-up threat if produced at the right moment.
runners_data.comment: Ran second two starts back but has looked out of sorts since, finishing seventh last time out, and her rating of 84 ranked eighth of thirteen suggests she faces a stiff task under 160 lb, despite having experience over today's trip and going.

runners_data.name: Urban War
runners_data.note: Hanlon's 8yo is a genuine hold-up horse shifted into the midfield map owing to an overcrowded rear division; 7 days since his last run, tp headgear, and a recent record of five consecutive finishes outside the frame on good ground (0W3P sim) all temper expectations significantly.
runners_data.comment: Urban War has run over today's trip and going, and our rating of 91 suggests more than his official mark of 88, but five winless starts in recent form and a trainer yet to land a winner in 20 attempts over the last fortnight make confidence hard to hold.

runners_data.name: Tomas O Maille
runners_data.note: A natural rear-ranger for Flannery who is unlikely to secure his preferred position in this compressed field; 38 days off, no headgear, and a form string of 0-9P9P tells its own story — the OR of 87 may flatter his current ability at this level.
runners_data.comment: Rated 95 and ranked second of 13 here, Tomas O Maille has run over today's trip and going, and 38 days between runs leaves him fresh enough to improve; the concern is a recent sequence of two pulled-up efforts and two ninths, leaving him winless in his last five starts.

runners_data.name: Calm Flight Ahead
runners_data.note: Rothwell's 5yo returns after a lengthy 83-day break wearing a hood; the finish-fade tag combined with just 1 qualified sim-going run from 5 attempts and a string of poor finishes (0000-P) means there is very little to encourage even if he finds a slot from the rear.
runners_data.comment: Calm Flight Ahead was pulled up last time out and has been winless in his last five starts, but he arrives lightly raced and unexposed with room to improve; 83 days between runs and 148 lb to carry are the key queries here.

runners_data.name: Invincible Oscar
runners_data.note: 260 days off the track is a very significant concern for Kelly's 5yo; the sim-going record is slim (0W0P from 3 runs), the finish-fade flag is noted, and returning after such an absence in a competitive handicap hurdle from a hold-up position is an extremely tall order.
runners_data.comment: Lightly raced and open to improvement, Invincible Oscar returns from a 260-day absence yet to score in recent starts, and connections will be hoping the layoff has freshened her for a more encouraging effort here.

runners_data.name: Granlahan
runners_data.note: McGuinness's consistent 4yo has placed three times from eight sim-going runs and notably finished third in a 18f good-ground hurdle just 10 days ago — the yard is in form (T14: 5/25) and Daniel King takes the ride; his hold-up role is genuine but the young age and placed consistency make him worth monitoring.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts and ranked ninth of 13 on our figures, Granlahan is hard to fancy at the weights, though he has experience over today's distance and going and was a close second last time out, just ten days ago.

runners_data.name: Tasmanian Girl
runners_data.note: Queally's mare showed a win from 13 sim-going runs and the yard is active (T14: 4/10); naturally a hold-up type displaced into midfield on the map, she carried headgear last time and the 6yo has mixed recent form (60-P96) — not without interest at a big price but the race shape is against her.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts, with a pulled-up among them, Tasmanian Girl arrives 16 days since her latest effort and ranks tenth of thirteen on our figures; experience over today's trip and going and a manageable turnaround are slim consolations for a mare so out of form.

runners_data.name: Wings Of Africa
runners_data.note: Lanigan's 5yo carries a finish-fade flag on top of a true rear-running style that cannot be accommodated at the back of this field; 12 days since last run, 0W0P from sim-going runs, and a recent form of P-068P make a serious impact very unlikely.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts and pulled up on two of those occasions, Wings Of Africa looks hard to fancy here, ranked well below the field on our figures; the one consolation is she has run over today's going before.

races.paceDynamic: William F Browne is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 13-runner field and, with no genuine rival likely to press him hard from the gates, he is set to control proceedings at a sustainable gallop around Sligo's tight, undulating track. The pace is unlikely to be scorching — one horse dictating on good ground over 2m1½f creates a compressed, tactical affair where the field will bunch together through the middle stages rather than string out. Horses racing prominently behind William F Browne — particularly Tradonthebay and Fremantle Doctor — are best placed to exploit a modest tempo, staying close enough to pounce if the leader weakens from the second-last. This race shape strongly favours prominent racers and hold-up types with a quick turn of foot, rather than deep closers who need a true end-to-end gallop to reel the field in. Several runners — Urban War, Tomas O Maille, Granlahan, Calm Flight Ahead, Invincible Oscar, Tasmanian Girl and Wings Of Africa — are genuine hold-up types redistributed into a midfield map position because the field is dominated by horses who prefer to race from the rear; of these, Granlahan and Bowgate Street carry the best credentials to actually threaten, though neither is guaranteed to secure their preferred spot.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Pace, Front Group Wins
scenarios.trigger: If William F Browne dictates an uncontested, moderate gallop and the race is not truly run, the first two or three home emerge from the front group.
scenarios.body: William F Browne sets a sustainable clip that denies closers the strong pace they need, and prominent stalkers like Tradonthebay and Fremantle Doctor travel sweetly into contention before the last two flights.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Leader Ties Up, One Closer Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If William F Browne's solo lead catches up with him in the final half-mile and he fades sharply from the second-last.
scenarios.body: A well-timed hold-up horse who has been produced with a late challenge benefits as the leader capitulates; Bowgate Street's strong course form (1W4P on good turf) and proven stamina at this distance make him the obvious danger.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Duel Quickens Race
scenarios.trigger: If Tradonthebay or another prominent type pushes up to challenge William F Browne before the turn in, injecting more genuine pace.
scenarios.body: A stronger gallop stretches the field and tests stamina, potentially undoing the leader earlier and rewarding horses with proven staying power like Bowgate Street and Tradonthebay who handles a strongly-run 20f+ trip.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaotic Cluster Finish
scenarios.trigger: If the compressed tactical race produces a wall of horses arriving together at the last with no clear winner emerging from the front.
scenarios.body: In a bunched finish every contender has a theoretical shot, but horses with finishing pace warnings — Alentejo, High Honour, Wings Of Africa — are at a significant disadvantage; Granlahan's consistent placed form and young age give him an each-way foothold.

watchPoints.text: William F Browne has blinkers fitted for the first time today — if they sharpen him into a more forceful early gallop than expected, the race tempo could lift and undermine his own front-running chance by the final flight.

Granlahan ran just 10 days ago and is four years old in a veteran-heavy field; if McGuinness has him fresh enough to produce another placed effort, a return to the frame is plausible given the trainer's recent 5/25 14-day strike rate.

Bowgate Street's 14 sim-going runs at 1W4P make him the most reliable course-conditions benchmark in the race — if O'Keeffe can position him closer than his usual hold-up role in the compressed pace scenario, he becomes a significant danger.

High Honour has not raced for 68 days and Invincible Oscar returns after 260 days off — both hold-up types with finish-fade flags; if either shows unexpected freshness the true pace picture could shift, but the form evidence does not invite confidence in either.

With seven genuine hold-up types squeezed into a midfield map, watch the early stages for traffic and crowding on Sligo's tight track — horses with prominent-race tendencies like Tradonthebay may move up earlier than ideal if the pace is modest.

races.name: Solar Generation Maiden Hurdle

runners_data.name: Godsend
runners_data.note: Strong winning form on Good ground (three of last four wins), but hold-up style means relying on others to set a searching pace — this controlled tempo is not ideal, and 18 days since last run is no concern.

runners_data.name: Mindyourheadmike
runners_data.note: The lone front-runner who controls everything from the front; Good-ground form is solid (1W1P from 3 sim-going runs) and apprentice allowance is a bonus, though whether he can sustain it over 2m4½f is the key question.

runners_data.name: Discrete
runners_data.note: Has headgear applied and a fall in recent form, raising jumping reliability concerns; ran twice on Good and failed to threaten on both occasions, making this a risk proposition at 9 days turnaround.

runners_data.name: Go To The Moon
runners_data.note: Prominent-style runner with headgear, lightly tried on Good ground (0W0P from 2 similar-going runs) but returns after 44 days; likely to sit just off Mindyourheadmike and could benefit if the pace is modest.

runners_data.name: Lengaruka
runners_data.note: Lightly raced and an unknown quantity beyond two runs, both on Good ground without threatening; the unknowns around his profile make him speculative, though 26 days since last run is fine.

runners_data.name: Seven Towers
runners_data.note: Consistent prominent racer with four placed efforts from six Good-ground starts — no wins but rarely far away; Keith Donoghue is a strong jockey booking and Cromwell's string is in decent form (4/14 last 14 days).

runners_data.name: Hadahi
runners_data.note: Four-year-old returning after 94 days with an unknown going profile, and an unseated rider in recent form; lightly raced profile makes him hard to assess, but the layoff and inexperience are meaningful flags.

runners_data.name: Kisuton Enki
runners_data.note: Jack Kennedy takes the ride for Gordon Elliott — always significant — and this horse has two placed efforts from Good-ground starts including a win on his last hurdles run; the 84-day break is the one note of caution, but the team and jockey combination demands respect.

races.paceDynamic: Mindyourheadmike is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 8-runner maiden hurdle over 2m4½f at Sligo on Good ground, and with no other prominent types likely to seriously challenge for the lead, he should dictate an uncontested, controlled tempo from the outset. Seven Towers and Go To The Moon will press forward into prominent positions just off the pace, but neither has the profile or inclination to take on Mindyourheadmike for the lead, meaning the gallop is likely to be measured and sustainable rather than searching. Kisuton Enki, a Jack Kennedy booking from the Elliott yard, brings proven hurdles form and will track the pace from a prominent berth, giving him every chance to pounce when it matters. This race shape — a single, uncontested front-runner setting a sensible tempo over a staying trip on Good ground — strongly favours prominent-to-tracking types who can travel smoothly through the race and produce a clean round of jumping, rather than hold-up horses who will need a strong pace to close into.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Lead, Trackers Strike
scenarios.trigger: If Mindyourheadmike bowls along at a fair but unextended gallop and the prominent-to-tracking types travel comfortably throughout.
scenarios.body: Mindyourheadmike sets a manageable tempo that keeps the race honest without burning off the closers too early, and horses who travel prominently and jump efficiently will arrive upsides at the second-last with a full tank. Kisuton Enki and Seven Towers, both proven at tracking a pace on Good ground, are ideally placed to assert from the home turn.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Holds On
scenarios.trigger: If Mindyourheadmike sets a genuinely slow early pace that lulls the field, then quickens approaching the straight to steal an unassailable advantage.
scenarios.body: With no rival willing to press him, Mindyourheadmike could dictate a falsely slow gallop before injecting pace in the home straight, turning the race into a flat sprint that catches hold-up horses cold. His Good-ground form record backs him and his apprentice rider Eoghan Finegan has the tactical freedom to execute this if the race unfolds quietly.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Swoop Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace quickens early enough to string the field out and the hold-up horses get a strong gallop to close into.
scenarios.body: Godsend, a winner four times and with strong Good-ground credentials, would be the primary beneficiary if the tempo is genuinely searching and the front rank fades in the final climb. However, hold-up tactics at Sligo on a moderate pace are a difficult recipe, limiting this scenario's likelihood.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos — Errors Shuffle Deck
scenarios.trigger: If jumping errors or fallers disrupt the race order and reshuffle positions significantly in the back straight.
scenarios.body: Discrete carries a headgear flag and has a fall in recent form, making jumping frailty a genuine possibility, while Hadahi's inexperience and 94-day absence adds further unpredictability. A scrambled race could allow a horse to slip the field unnoticed, but this depends on incidents outside the likely race flow.

watchPoints.text: Kisuton Enki — watch the Elliott/Kennedy combination closely; if this horse travels smoothly in a prominent position turning for home, he is the most dangerous in the race on paper.
Mindyourheadmike — if his gallop is genuinely slow and he quickens early in the straight, hold-up horses Godsend and Hadahi could find themselves with too much ground to make up.
Discrete — headgear plus a fall in recent form flags jumping frailty; watch at the early hurdles, as a mistake or exit could disrupt horses close behind.
Hadahi — 94-day absence and an unseated rider in the form string; watch in the parade ring and early in the race for signs of rustiness or greenness that could unsettle the race pattern.

Seven Towers — four consecutive placed runs on Good ground makes him a consistent each-way player; if he settles sweetly just off the pace, he may be the one to run into a place even if outclassed at the death.

races.name: McDermott Farm Machinery Handicap Hurdle

runners_data.name: Wild Mandate
runners_data.note: Seven-year-old who is the sole genuine pace-setter here, giving him a soft lead on Good ground that suits; his recent form (2nd at Gowran, fell/pulled up back steps) is mixed but the uncontested lead is his biggest asset, though Alan King's 7lb claim needs to work in harmony with a bold jumping display.
runners_data.comment: Won two starts back and has run over today's going, Wild Mandate arrives on a quick 17-day turnaround as the top-rated runner in the field; the pulled-up effort last time is the one question mark, but her class and going experience make her the one to beat.

runners_data.name: Laska Du Breuil
runners_data.note: Gavin Cromwell's five-year-old returned to winning form last time at Tipperary (1st, soft) and steps up to a longer trip where her hold-up style could suit if the gallop is honest; Keith Donoghue's experience in big fields is a major positive, though 83 days off and this step to 2m4½f are queries to respect.
runners_data.comment: Laska Du Breuil returns after 83 days off on the back of a win last time out, which is the clear positive, though a pulled up run two starts back raises a fitness question and our rating of 84 leaves him well held on paper in a field of 17.

runners_data.name: Phoenix Arizona
runners_data.note: Consistent hold-up type who has placed in four of his last five on Good ground at around this trip, giving him a solid profile for this surface; Thomas O'Connor's 7lb claim is a slight negative in a big-field tactical race, but the horse's ability to finish in the frame repeatedly makes him a place contender.
runners_data.comment: Phoenix Arizona arrives here in fine fettle after three placings in his last five starts, including a second last time out and a third two starts back, and has run over today's going before — the main risk is he remains yet to win in recent starts.

runners_data.name: Georginas Jet
runners_data.note: Five-year-old hold-up performer who won over 18f on Good and ran a tidy 3rd last time out; Jack Gilligan's 5lb claim adds value if the horse settles well in the large field, though he'll need a clear run from the rear in what shapes up as a congested finish.
runners_data.comment: Returned to form with a third last time out after a poor ninth two starts back, and she has run over today's distance and going before; the 158 lb burden is a stiff ask for a mare rated 88, and our rating of 84 ranks her sixth of seventeen.

runners_data.name: Love Like This
runners_data.note: Eight-year-old who won over 24f on Good ground in his last victory and has a consistent record at this trip-and-going combination; Brian Barry's 7lb claim is a consideration, but this is a horse who finds the line and his recent 4th at Killarney (25f, soft) keeps him honest.
runners_data.comment: Third three starts back shows she retains ability, but an unplaced run two starts back and a trainer in the midst of a 0-from-20 spell give real cause for caution; she has run over today's trip and going before, yet ranked seventh of seventeen, the weight of 158 lb looks a stiff ask.

runners_data.name: Ranting And Raven
runners_data.note: Four-year-old hold-up type for Cromwell with a modest recent form string, never finishing better than 6th in any of his last five; the Good ground is fine but he looks a horse to oppose rather than support in this competitive handicap.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts and ranked 10th of 17 on our rating, Ranting And Raven faces a stiff ask off 154 lb, though she has run over today's going before and the 27-day break leaves her fresh enough to outrun recent modest efforts.

runners_data.name: Beacon Bypass
runners_data.note: A true hold-up runner who tends to fade in the finish — his ground profile (all four recent runs on Good) is fine, but his race history shows consistent back-end fading; shunted into a midfield map position because of field congestion, not by design, which is an additional structural disadvantage.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and ranked 13 of 17 on our figures, Beacon Bypass has a significant gulf to bridge on ratings alone; 80 days off the track adds a fitness query, though he has run over today's going before.

runners_data.name: Sekakarma
runners_data.note: Nine-year-old whose natural instinct is to come from off the pace, but in a field this large he is likely to occupy a more forward position than he'd choose; his best recent effort was 2nd over 20f on Good, and Harry Sexton's 7lb claim suits the weights, though age and modest recent form limit expectations.
runners_data.comment: Sekakarma brings strong claims here, boasting experience over today's trip and going and returning on a quick 12-day turnaround in sound form, his runner-up last time out complemented by a rating of 88; the risk is that he remains winless in recent starts.

runners_data.name: Katie's Casper
runners_data.note: Seven-year-old hold-up horse who ran 2nd over 24f on Good and 5th twice at this trip — genuinely course-distance competent; Dermot McLoughlin saddles with 1 win in 7 over 14 days, and while the horse is able, being pushed into a midfield slot against his instinct costs him late-race momentum.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts, Katie's Casper at least showed promise with a second three starts back, though she has been unplaced most recently and carries a hefty 150 lb — going experience helps, but a turnaround is needed.

runners_data.name: Mother Ship
runners_data.note: Six-year-old Hanlon-trained hold-up type whose recent form (7th, 8th twice, pulled up) is poor, and the redistribution to midfield only compounds a horse who hasn't been finishing races off; Good ground is familiar but nothing in his profile suggests he's ready to reverse that slide.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts and carrying 149 lb for a trainer yet to land a winner in 20 attempts over the past fortnight, Mother Ship faces stiff headwinds, though she has run over today's distance and going before and a rating of 87 suggests some untapped potential.

runners_data.name: Gortmore Lady
runners_data.note: Ciaran Murphy's six-year-old (3 wins in 12 over 14 days from the trainer) ran 3rd and 7th recently and holds some interest; being squeezed into a midfield position rather than her natural hold-up spot is a minor concern, though any switching off problems (headgear: p) need monitoring early in such a large field.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts, Gortmore Lady does at least bring experience over today's trip and going, and a third two starts back shows she can hit the frame; however, a seventh last time out and a career-high 148 lb ask give pause for a mare ranked ninth of seventeen.

runners_data.name: Clever Court
runners_data.note: Five-year-old who won over 20f on Good last time, giving him the most relevant recent form boost in this field; P J Rothwell has 2 wins in 30 over 14 days which is modest, but the horse's 1W form on Good at a similar trip makes him one of the more interesting runners from deeper positions.

runners_data.name: El Arco
runners_data.note: Gordon Elliott's five-year-old returns from 146 days off, having run 5th over 26f on Good as his best Good-ground effort; the long absence and modest overall record make him hard to back with confidence, and Josh Williamson's 3lb claim doesn't compensate for the fitness doubt.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and ranked 16 of 17 on our figures, El Arco arrives after a 146-day absence carrying 144 lb, and while he has run over today's going before, there is precious little in his recent record to inspire confidence.

runners_data.name: Move It On Over
runners_data.note: Five-year-old with a fading pattern in his finishing and a modest Good-ground record (4th over 18f is his best); Philip Byrnes takes over and the horse's redistribution from true hold-up into midfield means he races structurally out of role — nothing in the profile screams danger.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and ranked 12 of 17 on our assessment, Move It On Over has distance and going experience to call upon, but the combination of a 144 lb burden and that patchy recent record — including an unseating — makes him a tough each-way proposition.

runners_data.name: Glaoinn An Airgead
runners_data.note: Eight-year-old whose form reads F0-0P0 and who fades in the finish — his Good-ground record at this trip (10th, 11th, 12th) is consistently poor; Daniel King takes over for James Barcoe but there is no angle in the data that makes this horse a realistic factor.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, with a pull-up and a fall among the recent finishes, Glaoinn An Airgead is hard to fancy at the foot of our rankings here; he does return on a quick turnaround with distance and going experience to his name, but that counts for little on this evidence.

runners_data.name: Max Time
runners_data.note: Nine-year-old prominent type who is flagged as a fader, a dangerous combination for a horse who could be drawn into a pace battle with Wild Mandate; his Good-ground record includes a 4th but the bulk of his runs end in a pull-up or near the rear, and Joshua Halford's 7lb claim cannot fix a tendency to stop.
runners_data.comment: Max Time has pulled up in three of his last five starts and is winless in that span, making him very difficult to fancy ranked 14 of 17 on our figures; he has run over today's trip and going before, and 15 days since his last outing suggests he is at least fit to run his race.

runners_data.name: Hob's Angel
runners_data.note: Ten-year-old with a genuine winning record on Good (won twice in last five) and an honest placing profile for James Barcoe; no jockey declared is a concern for race-day information, but the horse's 2nd and 3rd runs in recent form show he stays 20-24f on this surface and can be competitive at the right price.
runners_data.comment: Ranked 15 of 17 on our figures and weighted at 147 lb, Hob's Angel faces a stiff task, and a sixth last time out does little to inspire confidence; she has run over today's trip and going before, and a win in her last five starts shows ability is there somewhere.

runners_data.name: Firstupbestdressed
runners_data.note: Six-year-old hold-up runner who fades and whose recent form includes two unseated-rider runs before a modest 3rd; Gary McGill's operation shows 0 wins in 1 over 14 days and the horse's pattern of stopping in finishes is not corrected by the midfield mapping — difficult to recommend.
runners_data.comment: Firstupbestdressed shaped with promise when third two starts back and has run over today's trip and going, with our rating of 88 suggesting he holds strong claims as a leading danger in this field; the main risk is that he remains winless in recent starts.

races.paceDynamic: Wild Mandate is the lone confirmed front-runner in this 18-runner handicap hurdle, and with no genuine challenger willing to press from the front, he is set to bowl along at a controlled, self-dictated tempo over the 2m4½f trip on Good ground. Max Time carries a prominent tag but is flagged as a fader and is unlikely to apply meaningful pressure, meaning Wild Mandate can find a rhythm without ever being forced to empty his tank early. The field behind is almost entirely comprised of hold-up and midfield types — Beacon Bypass, Sekakarma, Katie's Casper, Mother Ship, Gortmore Lady, Clever Court and others are all genuine hold-up horses who cannot all settle deep as is their nature in a field this large, and several will be forced into unnatural tracking positions through no choice of their own; Wild Mandate and Laska Du Breuil are best placed to capitalise on their natural roles. The race shape — a single uncontested leader, sustainable gallop, large field bottling up the closers — strongly favours horses who can track the pace without burning energy early, turning Good ground into an asset for those comfortable making a forward move three out rather than relying on a late charge through a wall of traffic.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Wild Mandate Leads Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Wild Mandate sets a controlled solo gallop and the compressed hold-up pack fails to land a clean blow from deep.
scenarios.body: Wild Mandate rolls along without pressure, the tempo stays honest but not brutal, and a prominent or close-tracking runner picks off the tired stragglers from the second-last; closers face traffic in a bunched finish leaving tactical riders the edge.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Cuts Through
scenarios.trigger: If the pace proves genuinely honest enough to string out the field and one hold-up runner finds a clear passage from the rear.
scenarios.body: A legitimate closer manages to thread through the large field in the home straight, arriving with a late surge as the pace-set front group ties up; this requires both a true enough gallop and fortunate jumping gaps.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Tactical Mess, Prominent Wins
scenarios.trigger: If mid-race jostling in the big field disrupts rhythm and a horse tracking just off Wild Mandate pounces two out.
scenarios.body: With 18 runners on a tight Sligo circuit, crowding and interference is a real threat — a horse sitting third or fourth and jumping cleanly gains a decisive break on the bunched remainder.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Faders Vulnerable
scenarios.trigger: If Wild Mandate is taken on or quickens too hard early and the whole field converges in a chaotic scramble up the home straight.
scenarios.body: A truly-run race exposes faders like Max Time and Beacon Bypass badly, and a horse with natural freshness or an unexposed profile capitalises in a rough finish; this scenario is low-probability given the lone-leader dynamic.

watchPoints.text: Wild Mandate's jumping must be monitored closely — if he sprawls at any of the early hurdles, the controlled lead evaporates instantly and the race shape collapses entirely, shifting advantage to hold-up horses who are then gifted a muddled race.

With 18 runners on the tight Sligo circuit, congestion at the top of the home straight is near-certain — watch for Beacon Bypass, Sekakarma and Katie's Casper being severely hampered as the true hold-up horses try to find gaps that may not exist.

Max Time is tagged as a fader but carries a prominent style — if he attempts to challenge Wild Mandate for the lead early and is allowed to do so, the pace could lift into territory that burns out both horses and opens the door for a late finisher at bigger odds.

Laska Du Breuil is returning from 83 days off for the in-form Cromwell yard (4 wins in 14 over 14 days) — watch for how sharply she moves through gears two out, as a race-rusty performance early could give way to a strong staying finish if her stamina kicks in.

Clever Court's recent Good-ground win over 20f is the standout recent form piece among the midfield/hold-up group — monitor whether Shane O'Callaghan (3lb claim) positions him closer than his usual hold-up profile to take advantage of any gaps left by the compressed field.

races.name: Francie 'Banger' Burns Handicap Hurdle

runners_data.name: In For The Night
runners_data.note: An eight-year-old hold-up horse trained by Conor O'Dwyer and ridden by his claim-carrying son Charlie (3lb); has a strong record on Good ground (sim-going 12/15) and won over 19f on Good last time, making this trip and surface squarely in his wheelhouse — 26 days fresh is fine.
runners_data.comment: In For The Night landed a win last time out and arrives here 26 days later in solid nick, with experience over today's trip and conditions working in his favour; 166 lb is no featherweight, but his current form makes him our pick from the field.

runners_data.name: In The Minus
runners_data.note: Won last time out over 21f on Good and returns after just 13 days, suggesting connections are confident; Brian Cawley's yard is 1/1 in the 14-day window, and a four-year-old who is still lightly raced holds improvement potential at this trip and surface.
runners_data.comment: In The Minus bounced back to winning ways last time out and, carrying 163 lb fresh off a 13-day turnaround with experience of today's trip and conditions, he arrives in fine fettle; the risk is that his prior four runs yielded three fifths and an unplaced effort, suggesting consistency remains the query.

runners_data.name: Drombane
runners_data.note: Prominent racer for Willie Mullins, who is 12/27 in the 14-day period — a strong yard angle; tied for second on two recent Good-ground starts, though course form over softer ground is mixed, and he carries a hood (hg:t) that has been seen before.
runners_data.comment: Drombane shaped with plenty of promise when second two starts back and again four starts back, and with his trainer firing at 44% over the past fortnight, the conditions look right for this 108-rated gelding to go close; the risk is that he has gone winless in his last five starts.

runners_data.name: Harpy Eagle
runners_data.note: Won over 20f on Good 11 days ago for Paddy Cody (7lb claim), giving this run a very quick turnaround; prominent style suits a steady-paced race and Good-ground form is solid (sim-going 10/13), though the short recovery period is worth monitoring.
runners_data.comment: Harpy Eagle won last time out and has experience of today's trip and conditions, but his two starts before that brought a pair of sixth-place finishes and he carries a hefty 157 lb which could blunt that momentum.

runners_data.name: Tangara Bay
runners_data.note: Natural hold-up type from Peter Fahey's yard who has not shown great Good-ground form (sim-going 2/6, no wins or places); best effort came on Soft, and the surface here is a concern, though the trip at 19f suits his stamina profile.
runners_data.comment: Tangara Bay won two starts back and has experience of both today's trip and going, arriving here 21 days fresh and carrying 156 lb — that weight burden is the one factor she must overcome to confirm herself a leading danger.

runners_data.name: Bossy Bird
runners_data.note: Capable hold-up performer who won over 20f on Good and placed on that surface, giving genuine pace credentials — the key caveat is that with so many hold-up types in this field, he is likely to be racing closer to the pace than he wants, which tempers his chance (style-fit 0.92).
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts but that second two runs back shows ability, and having run over today's trip and going is a plus; the 155 lb burden is the chief concern for a mare ranked sixth of eleven here.

runners_data.name: Crystabel
runners_data.note: The lone front-runner for John Patrick Ryan, who is 0/20 in 14 days — a cold yard stat; her five recent runs are all on Good and she won over 18f last time, so track and trip suit, and she will dictate terms from the front without pressure.
runners_data.comment: Ranked ninth of eleven on our figures and representing a trainer without a winner in twenty attempts over the past fortnight, Crystabel is hard to fancy at the weights despite her win three starts back and a third two starts back, and going experience counts for little here.

runners_data.name: Coolboy Christy
runners_data.note: Has a headgear flag (hg:p) and has been running consistently without winning since a 2024 break; a hold-up horse who will be closer to midfield than he naturally wants — his 0W1P sim-going record and redistribution flag combine to temper expectations here.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and ranked eighth of eleven here, Coolboy Christy faces a stiff ask under 148 lb, though he has run over today's trip and going before and returns on a sharp 17-day turnaround that at least suggests fitness.

runners_data.name: Midnight Eagle
runners_data.note: Held-up runner from Andrew McNamara's yard who has placed twice at 17f on Good but is flagged as fading in the finish, which in a 2m4½f test is a real concern; racing in a more prominent position than ideal (redistributed) further complicates his chance.
runners_data.comment: Midnight Eagle has been placed third last time out and second two starts back, showing she finds the frame without quite getting her head in front, and while she has run over today's trip and going before, carrying 148 lb looks the stiffest ask for a mare yet to win in her last five starts.

runners_data.name: Ladiam
runners_data.note: A nine-year-old prominent-style horse who carries a hood (hg:t) and has an outstanding sim-going record (14/15), though his wins are few (1W7P) and he has been running over longer trips; comes back from just 9 days, the freshest horse in the field — connections clearly think he is in form.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts and ranked tenth of eleven on our figures, Ladiam faces a stiff task here, though she does bring fitness from a run nine days ago and has experience of today's trip and going to call on.

runners_data.name: Dream Shaper
runners_data.note: Prominent runner with a hood (hg:t) who won over 19f on Good and has placed in this type of company; for a 7lb claimer (Joshua Halford) and a lightly-worked trainer (0/3 in 14 days), he arrives with modest support angles, though Good-ground form (10/15) is acceptable.
runners_data.comment: Dream Shaper was a winner two starts back but has since finished eighth, and ranked last of eleven on our figures he faces a stiff ask here, though he returns after just 17 days carrying 143 lb with both distance and going experience in his favour.

races.paceDynamic: Crystabel is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no other genuine pace horse to challenge her, she will bowl along from the front at a controlled, sustainable gallop on Good ground at Sligo over 2m4½f. Drombane, Harpy Eagle, Ladiam, and Dream Shaper will fill the prominent slots behind her, creating an orderly procession rather than a pace battle. The hold-up brigade — In For The Night, In The Minus, Tangara Bay, Bossy Bird, Coolboy Christy, and Midnight Eagle — represent more off-the-pace types than this race can accommodate at the rear; Bossy Bird, Coolboy Christy, and Midnight Eagle are redistributed into the midfield map, meaning they will be racing ahead of their natural comfort zone and may not get the late cover they need. This race shape — a single, uncontested leader setting a measured tempo — strongly favours hold-up horses with a genuine late kick, provided they travel smoothly in a compact midfield and can find daylight at the second-last; horses with proven Good-ground form at this sort of trip who can quicken off a steady gallop hold the clearest tactical edge.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Crystabel Dictates Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Crystabel is allowed to stride on at her own pace and the field settles into a single-file procession behind the prominent group.
scenarios.body: Crystabel sets a controlled tempo that keeps the race honest but never brutal, and the energy-efficient hold-up horses In For The Night and In The Minus are delivered with momentum at the second-last to pick her off.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Runners Grind It Out
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent quartet press Crystabel harder than expected and turn it into a test of stamina from three out.
scenarios.body: A grinding pace suits the more relentless staying types who race in the first half of the field; Drombane, under Brian Hayes for Mullins, and Harpy Eagle, who landed a recent win on Good ground, have the cruising speed to capitalise if the leaders hit the wall.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Closers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses from three out and true hold-up types — those not pushed out of role — finish powerfully from the back.
scenarios.body: In The Minus, a recent winner who handles Good ground and has been running off 13 days, can deliver a sustained run late if a gap opens; Tangara Bay, with moderate Good-ground form but natural hold-up ability, could also pick up scraps.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Redistributed Types Outrun Role
scenarios.trigger: If Bossy Bird, Coolboy Christy, or Midnight Eagle adapt to their enforced midfield position and use it to box-seat advantage rather than being disadvantaged by it.
scenarios.body: This is a low-probability shape because all three are flagged as racing out of their natural role and carry reduced style-fit scores; Midnight Eagle is further flagged as a finisher who fades, making this scenario structurally weak.

watchPoints.text: Watch whether any of the prominent quartet — Drombane, Harpy Eagle, Ladiam or Dream Shaper — pushes Crystabel for the lead early; if even one applies pressure, the tempo lifts and the race shape shifts from Scenario A to Scenario B entirely.
Harpy Eagle ran just 11 days ago and now faces a step back up in trip; if he ties up in the closing stages after a prominent run, he could bring down the finishing positions of horses tracking him.

Bossy Bird, Coolboy Christy, and Midnight Eagle will all be racing closer to the pace than their natural style demands — monitor whether any of the three manages to drop back and find cover, or whether they are caught in no-man's land mid-race.

Crystabel's trainer John Patrick Ryan is 0/20 in the past 14 days — a long cold run — so note whether she is ridden with any unusual instructions (held up, ridden cold early) that might signal the yard is trying something different tactically.

The Going is confirmed Good through six earlier races on the card — no meaningful deterioration — which validates all the sim-going Good-ground form assessments and particularly benefits In For The Night and In The Minus, both with strong recent Good-ground returns.

races.name: Adare Manor Opportunity Handicap Hurdle

runners_data.name: Ringdufferin
runners_data.note: A natural hold-up operator with fair recent form on Good ground (2nd at 20f, 6th at 22f), likely to race at the back of the field naturally; 10 from 15 runs on similar going with two places suggests solid surface fit, though 14 of 24f last time out hints stamina is tested at this 3m1½f trip.|
runners_data.comment: Rated highest in the field and carrying 166 lb, Ringdufferin arrives on a going he has experience of and shaped with promise when second two starts back — the weight burden, however, is the chief concern for a gelding yet to win in his last five starts.

runners_data.name: Luck Between Us
runners_data.note: Won last time out over 20f on Good, trained by Donncha Duggan who has a live 14-day record (1/5), and this six-year-old has strong similar-going stats (5 from 8, 1W3P); a genuine hold-up horse that should get a clear run from the rear and represents one of the more in-form profiles in this race.|
runners_data.comment: Luck Between Us won last time out but that sole victory in his last five starts highlights some inconsistency, and a rating of 105 suggests he faces stiffer company here; he has experience of today's going and returns after 34 days off carrying 165 lb.

runners_data.name: Dorans Law
runners_data.note: Ran just nine days ago and carries headgear (tp), but the trainer P J Rothwell has been busy and productive (2/30 in 14 days); the horse's recent history is almost entirely on Good ground (13 from 15 sim-going, 1W5P) and the 3m1½f trip stretches his usual range slightly, though a hold-up style suits if the pace holds genuine.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, Dorans Law nonetheless shaped with promise when second two starts back, and returning on a quick nine-day turnaround he encounters familiar distance and going conditions; carrying 162 lb is the query, but his profile makes him our pick here.

runners_data.name: Cornmarket
runners_data.note: The only confirmed prominent racer outside the two front-runners, giving this seven-year-old a tactical advantage if it can track the leaders without being swamped; Cullen's runner has shown form at 26f (2nd) and Good ground record is decent (10 from 15), though the blinkers flag a trainer seeking more from him and recent finishes have been moderate.|
runners_data.comment: Cornmarket has run over today's trip and going and arrives fit on a 13-day turnaround, with a second three starts back suggesting he retains ability; carrying 161 lb, however, is the chief concern for a gelding yet to score in recent starts.

runners_data.name: Keep Em Quite
runners_data.note: A genuine confirmed front-runner who has been out just nine days, trained by Cian Collins (0/13 in 14-day window, so form rather than yard momentum carries the case); Good ground form is limited (3 from 5) but the horse's role as pace-setter means it shapes the race for everyone else regardless of its own winning chance.|
runners_data.comment: Placed second last time out and lively enough on his day, Keep Em Quite has run over today's going before and returns on a quick nine-day turnaround; winless in his last five starts, though, and carrying 160 lb as a seventh-ranked runner makes the upside hard to gauge.

runners_data.name: Ilbdare
runners_data.note: Won over 26f on Good last season for Mark Michael McNiff and has solid similar-going form (12 from 15, 2W5P); in truth a hold-up horse who will want to come from off the pace, but with so many hold-up types in the field it is unlikely to secure its preferred rear position — the redistribution to midfield reflects genuine positional pressure rather than a change of style.|
runners_data.comment: Ilbdare won last time out but has been below his best through the rest of recent starts, and 71 days off the track introduces a fitness query; he has run over today's trip and going before, though 159 lb is a stiff burden to carry back to form.

runners_data.name: Mr Dibbs
runners_data.note: Cromwell's runner won over 26f on Good and was second over 20f, giving him the best distance credentials of the hold-up brigade; out 15 days and wearing blinkers, the trainer's 14-day record is strong (4/14) and his similar-going profile (11 from 15, 2W4P) makes him a serious contender if the hold-up game works from an honest pace.|
runners_data.comment: Mr Dibbs bounced back to winning ways two starts back and returns on a quick 15-day turnaround with experience of both today's trip and going in his favour; the main concern is whether that eighth last time out signals a return to inconsistency.

runners_data.name: Sallap
runners_data.note: Has won twice on Good ground at 22f and carries a flagged tendency to fade in the finish, which is a real concern in a 3m1½f stamina test even with a contested pace; in reality a hold-up horse forced to race in a congested midfield due to the weight of similar types, and the finishing fade flag combined with the positional squeeze reduces confidence in a late flourish.|
runners_data.comment: Sallap has back-to-back wins in her recent starts to her name, but she sits second-bottom of our rankings in this field and carries a hefty 157 lb, making her hard to fancy despite a fifth last time out and going experience.

runners_data.name: Tango Theatre
runners_data.note: An 11-year-old confirmed front-runner who has won over 24f on Good and is trained by McConnell (3/27 in 14 days, active yard); wearing a tongue-tie and visor and clearly needs to lead, but at this age and weight (151lbs) against a younger rival in Keep Em Quite, the worry is whether he can sustain the front-running role or simply tows them into a race for another.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts and ranked ninth of twelve on our figures, Tango Theatre faces a stiff ask at 151 lb, though she has run over today's trip and going before and shaped with some promise when second last time out.

runners_data.name: Hey Babbs
runners_data.note: A hold-up horse returning from 123 days off — the longest layoff in the field — for Dermot McLoughlin (1/7 in 14 days), and while Good-ground form shows a third at 24f, the extended absence raises fitness questions over 3m1½f; the field's depth of hold-up types means it won't find its natural position easily, and class at OR=93 is modest.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts, including two pulls up, Hey Babbs arrives after a 123-day absence carrying 150 lb and ranked tenth of twelve on our figures — the third last time out offers slim encouragement, but the overall profile makes her very hard to fancy.

runners_data.name: The Little Yank
runners_data.note: An 11-year-old veteran who has run consistently at 25f on Good (two thirds in last two), but question marks litter the earlier form (?/20f, ?/23f, ?/21f) and the blinkers plus hold-up style mean positional compromise is likely; in a field this congested with hold-up horses, a runner at OR=92 with limited upside finds little margin for error.|
runners_data.comment: Twice placed third in his last two starts after a run of pull-ups, The Little Yank arrives on an 11-day turnaround with distance and going experience to call on, yet he remains winless in recent starts and a trainer in the depths of a 0-from-20 spell is a significant concern.

runners_data.name: Strong Contender
runners_data.note: Won last time over 24f on Good which is relevant and recent (12 days), but OR=88 is the lowest in the race and four of the last five runs on Good ground have been poor (8th, 7th, 13th, 13th) before that win; genuine hold-up profile but forced into a midfield position by the weight of similar types — trainer Lee has modest recent figures (1/2 in 14 days, small sample).|
runners_data.comment: Ranked bottom of the field on our figures and a mare whose recent form reads mostly as unplaced finishes, Strong Contender is hard to recommend despite a win last time out and previous experience of today's going.

races.paceDynamic: Keep Em Quite and Tango Theatre are the two confirmed front-runners and will contest the lead from the outset over this 3m1½f trip on Good ground at Sligo, creating an honest, contested gallop rather than a mutualy agreed dawdle. With two genuine pace horses pushing each other along, the race is likely to be run at a true clip throughout, which will test the stamina of anything keen or free early. This shape — a contested, even-tempo lead over a stiff staying trip — strongly favours resolute hold-up horses with proven stamina at this sort of distance on Good ground, who can travel economically behind the pace and produce a sustained late challenge. The field holds more genuine hold-up types than the map can accommodate at the rear: Ilbdare, Sallap, Hey Babbs, The Little Yank and Strong Contender have all been redistributed to midfield, with Ringdufferin, Luck Between Us, Dorans Law and Mr Dibbs the hold-up runners most likely to actually race closer to their natural position and arrive fresh for the finish.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Contested Lead, Staying Test
scenarios.trigger: If Keep Em Quite and Tango Theatre set a genuine contested gallop and the pace holds honest throughout, burning out the prominent brigade.
scenarios.body: The two front-runners press each other across the 3m1½f trip on Good ground, steadily raising the stamina bar and emptying the tank of anything pressed into a prominent role against its nature; true hold-up horses who can travel economically and pick up late are the main beneficiaries.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Dominates Alone
scenarios.trigger: If Tango Theatre or Keep Em Quite surrenders the front early, leaving one uncontested leader to control tempo and steal a march.
scenarios.body: A single front-runner sets its own fractions, softening the race into a comfortable gallop that allows it to conserve energy and sprint clear before the hold-up horses can organise a serious challenge; at 3m1½f, a horse that dictates on its own terms at Sligo is genuinely dangerous.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Grinder Stays On
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuine but not extreme, and a prominent-tracking type settles just off the leaders and grinds relentlessly through the final mile.
scenarios.body: Cornmarket, the only confirmed prominent-style runner outside the two leaders, is best placed to exploit this scenario, tracking the front pair without overcommitting and wearing them down from two out; at 3m1½f on Good ground Sligo, the ability to travel smoothly in the leading group without burning early energy is the key asset.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Closers Pounce Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses in the final mile and the front-runners tie up, leaving room for hold-up horses to burst through.
scenarios.body: Several of the nominal hold-up runners — Ilbdare, Sallap, Hey Babbs — are displaced from their natural rear position by the weight of hold-up types in this field, meaning a true late flourish depends on horses racing somewhat out of role and arriving wide or short of room; with STYLE_FIT discounts applied across those redistributed types, this scenario is the least reliable despite the contested gallop seemingly setting it up.

watchPoints.text: Keep Em Quite and Tango Theatre will contest the lead immediately — watch whether either capitulates early, as the dominant pace-setter in a two-horse duel gains a significant advantage if the other drops away before halfway.

Sallap is flagged as a horse that fades in the finish, and at 3m1½f with a contested gallop, any move to challenge from midfield must come before the final hurdle or the fade tendency is likely to cost it the race.

Ilbdare, Hey Babbs and The Little Yank are all genuine hold-up horses compressed into a midfield position by field composition — watch the early quarter-mile to see if any manage to drop away naturally to the rear, which would restore their preferred race shape.

Mr Dibbs with Cromwell saddling (4/14 in 14-day window) and a won at 26f on Good is the hold-up runner most likely to arrive fresh and organised at the business end — watch his position at the third-last as an indicator of whether the hold-up profile will fire.

Cornmarket is the lone prominent type between the leaders and the hold-up pack — watch whether Alan King (claiming 4lb) can settle him in a ground-saving position tracking the front pair, as his ability to travel smoothly from that slot is the key to whether Scenario C develops.

races.name: WTW Willis Insurance Brokers Flat Race

runners_data.name: Bairdin
runners_data.comment: Winless in recent starts, Bairdin has nonetheless run over today's going before and returns after a 34-day break carrying 164 lb, with a rating of 70 suggesting he holds genuine claims among this field; the main concern is that sole recent run ended in an eighth.

runners_data.name: Conor'salwaysright
runners_data.comment: Conor'salwaysright catches the eye on fitness, stepping back up having run just 15 days ago, and his rating of 88 ranks him second among the eight runners here; the chief concern is that he is winless in recent starts and must find improvement on that fifth last time out.

runners_data.name: Gruncle
